newsitem.title: USA: Morgan sees AMD profitable from Q1 on.
newsitem.headline: Morgan sees AMD profitable from Q1 on.

text.p: Morgan Stanley analyst John Marren said he rated Advanced Micro Devices Inc as "outperform" in initiating coverage today because he believes the company's soon-to-be-released K6 chip "will drive big revenues and earnings in the next few years."

"They'll be profitable in Q1 1997 and not look back, in my opinion," Marren said of Advanced Micro, which has lost money for several quarters. It is expected today to report a loss of $0.55 for the 1996 year and a fourth quarter loss of $0.19 a share, according to a consensus tallied by First Call Corp.
Advanced Micro was up 2-1/4 to 29-7/8 late in the session.
Earlier, Advanced Micro hit a high of 30-7/8.

Marren expects Advanced Micro will produce four million to five million K6 chips in 1997, driving 40 percent revenue growth in 1997. The K6 is a microprocessor with capabilities designed to be comparable to Intel Corp's Pentium Pro with multimedia extensions. Advanced Micro expects to start shipping K6 this quarter.
Marren estimates Advanced Micro will earn $1.65 a share in 1997, which compares with a First Call mean estimate for 1997 of $0.81 a share, and $3.50 a share in 1998.
"My recommendation is not based on this past quarter," Marren said of the fourth quarter.
He estimates Advanced Micro will report a loss of $0.10 a share for the fourth quarter, compared with a profit of $0.07 a share in 1995's fourth quarter.
